key_insight: Inference weights are read-only and identical across replicas, so O(1) copies per pod suffice; broadcasting could free replica HBM for KV cache.
killer_doubt: Each replica still ingests all weights every step (~2-8 TB/s each) over a bus far slower than local HBM; TP/EP sharding already keeps one weight copy per scale-up domain.
decisive_experiment: Model a 70B decode pod: per-GPU ingest bandwidth, tokens/s and KV capacity for 8-way broadcast versus TP=8 sharding at batch 1-256, with real NVLink/CPO link budgets. Spreadsheet plus simulator, under $20k.
prior_art: Phase B N-80; R12 reviews of I-05406, I-03120, I-00277; Cerebras MemoryX/SwarmX weight broadcast; NVLink SHARP multicast; Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407).

key_insight: Wide, slow, short-reach LPDDR on cheap organic substrate trades bandwidth density for cost, sidestepping TSVs and CoWoS; a valid capacity tier beside or instead of HBM.
killer_doubt: LPDDR5X dies are x32, so 1024 bits need ~32 dies (~2,000 mm2) within 3 mm of the ASIC; ~10 native-speed dies give ~400 GB/s, a third of one HBM3E stack.
decisive_experiment: Floorplan and signal-integrity study: place LPDDR5X dies around a 600 mm2 ASIC on mSAP HDI, simulate 2.5-9.6 Gb/s channels, and compare GB/s per mm of shoreline and $/GB/s against HBM3E. Under $50k.
prior_art: Apple M-series Ultra ~1024-bit in-package LPDDR5 (~800 GB/s); NVIDIA Grace LPDDR5X; SK hynix LLW for Apple R1; Eliyan HBM-on-organic; JEDEC Wide I/O 2.

key_insight: Same coaxial in-hole 2T0C as I-03474. Its extra value, reusing depreciated 3D-NAND etch, ALD and staircase tools for DRAM-class bits, is merged into I-03474's review.
killer_doubt: One word plane per tier leaves the inner read channel a 100-segment series string: ~20-100 nA of string current means ~0.5-5 us sensing, NAND latency rather than DRAM's 10-100 ns.
decisive_experiment: Covered by I-03474: TCAD of a 16-100 tier string, then a 4-tier university-fab coupon measuring string current, unselected-cell pass margin and write disturb.
prior_art: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 1T1C/3T0C on a NAND-like process (2025, TCAD only; via search snippet); IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C; Phase B N-43.

key_insight: LLM decode activates every weight row each ~10-50 ms step, restoring cells for free. Weight-only DRAM can delete refresh and be binned or designed to a 16 ms retention spec.
killer_doubt: Cs is sized mainly by the Cs/Cbl sense ratio, not leak-down, so a 4x shorter window saves perhaps 1.2-1.5x in Cs, not 3x; refresh costs only ~5-20% of bandwidth.
decisive_experiment: With DRAM Bender/SoftMC on DDR5 and HBM parts at 85-95 C, disable refresh under a weight-sweep pattern at 16-64 ms; map failing rows and the retention-yield gain over the 64 ms spec. Under $100k.
prior_art: Smart Refresh (Ghosh and Lee, MICRO 2007) skips refresh for recently activated rows; RANA (ISCA 2018) uses DNN data lifetimes to cut eDRAM refresh.

key_insight: Growth-defined vertical doping profiles could set every tier's channel in one deposition step, trading lithography for chemistry; the instinct matches deposition-defined tier economics.
killer_doubt: VLS reservoir effects smear axial junctions over ~the wire diameter (20-40 nm), versus 25 nm segments; Au is a mid-gap leakage killer; 16 series transistors form a string, not cells.
decisive_experiment: Grow 40 nm Al- or Cu-catalysed Si wires with 4 dopant switches; measure junction abruptness by APT/SIMS and gate-all-around leakage per segment. University CVD, ~$150k; stop if transitions exceed 10 nm.
prior_art: Lieber (Harvard) axial-heterostructure nanowires; Lund University vertical nanowire GAA MOSFETs; IBM VLS Si nanowire work (training knowledge).

key_insight: Self-assembled parallel lamellae plus sequential infiltration synthesis could create many insulator/semiconductor tiers in one coat, replacing ~100 depositions with chemistry.
killer_doubt: A 12 nm period leaves ~6 nm per channel and no room for gate, dielectric and wordline (~30-60 nm per tier); per-layer staircase contacts at 12 nm pitch are unmanufacturable.
decisive_experiment: Coat a 20-period high-chi lamellar film, infiltrate In2O3 and AlOx, then TEM-check layer continuity and measure Hall mobility of buried infiltrated layers. ~$100k; stop if mobility is below 1 cm2/Vs.
prior_art: Argonne SIS (Darling, Elam); Brookhaven CFN SIS-derived ZnO transistors; parallel-lamella BCP films. No BCP-defined memory tiers found (training knowledge).

key_insight: With ~1000 s gain-cell retention, refresh power for a 16 Gb array falls to ~1 uW, so a package-level isotope source could make volatile memory persistent.
killer_doubt: Periphery standby (charge pumps, references, oscillator) typically draws ~10-100 uW versus betavoltaic tens of nW to ~100 uW; persistence is niche, and NVDIMM supercap-to-NAND already provides it.
decisive_experiment: Power-gate a gain-cell test array with burst refresh every 300-1000 s; measure average standby power against a commercial tritium or Ni-63 cell's output over a week at 85 C. ~$100k.
prior_art: City Labs NanoTritium betavoltaics pitched for SRAM/RTC retention; Betavolt BV100 Ni-63 cell; NVDIMM-N supercap backup to NAND (training knowledge).

key_insight: Wide-gap channels push off-current toward retention of hours. The coaxial in-hole geometry duplicates I-03474, so only the Ga2O3 channel choice is new.
killer_doubt: Oxide 2T0C already reaches >1,000 s (~30,000 s passivated), limited by traps and gate leakage, not bandgap; amorphous ALD Ga2O3 mobility is likely <1 cm2/Vs, slowing writes.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate planar ALD amorphous Ga2O3 and IGZO TFTs side by side at <=400 C; compare mobility, the Ioff floor via 2T0C retention at 85 C, and PBTI. University fab, ~$150k.
prior_art: Coaxial family: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 3T0C (TCAD; via search snippet), IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C, Phase B N-43; university Ga2O3 TFT research.

key_insight: One hole etch per 100 tiers, with per-tier recessed storage rings (like Micron's floating-gate recess), could give NAND layer economics to a transistor-written, capacitorless, high-endurance DRAM-class cell.
killer_doubt: Read and write paths are both series strings: ~100 IGZO segments give ~20-100 nA and ~0.5-5 us reads, and writing tier k rewrites every tier above it: NAND-like.
decisive_experiment: Use TCAD/SPICE to compare three topologies (series string, 3D-AND multi-pillar, two planes per tier) for read latency, density at 100 tiers and disturb. Then build a 4-tier IGZO coupon to measure string current and ring coupling. ~$400k.
prior_art: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 1T1C/3T0C on a NAND-like process (2025, TCAD only; via search snippet); IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C; Macronix 3D AND; Phase B N-43.

key_insight: Si thickness set by deposited nitride, not epitaxy, gives SOI-like c-Si tiers at NAND stack cost. Only transistors beside the seed slot need c-Si (~100-200 nm of growth).
killer_doubt: Precursor starvation and facet/twin defects in ~20 nm-tall tunnels across 100+ tiers; upper tiers seed late from a 6-7 um slot fill. Superlattices may already reach ~120 layers.
decisive_experiment: Build 8-16 oxide/nitride tiers on Si, cut seed slots, strip the nitride, grow selective Si (DCS/HCl) laterally 100-500 nm; get TEM defect counts per tier plus gated-diode leakage tails at 85 C. ~$500k with an epi partner.
prior_art: TC Lab patent family: nitride-strip tunnels filled by confined epitaxial overgrowth for stacked thyristors (via search snippet); Purdue CLSEG/CELO; Samsung/imec Si/SiGe superlattice 3D DRAM.

key_insight: In 3D DRAM, defects cluster by tier (plane shorts, voids). Coding orthogonal to tiers turns a dead tier into one erasure per codeword rather than a dead block.
killer_doubt: Two spare tiers per 32 already tolerate 1% tier-defect rates (block yield ~99.5%); vertical-bitline arrays cannot read 32 tiers in one activation without bitline collisions.
decisive_experiment: Run a Monte Carlo of tier-, line- and cell-level defect maps for a 32-128 tier array, comparing die yield and area for tier sparing, row/column redundancy plus ECC, and cross-tier codes. Software, under $30k.
prior_art: Micron RAIN parity across NAND planes and dies; Chipkill symbol codes; HBM on-die ECC; 3D NAND bad-block management with spare blocks (training knowledge).

key_insight: Swapping Fowler-Nordheim for low-voltage direct tunneling could cut write voltage and wear in NAND-tool charge-trap strings; the room-temperature quasi-volatile version is Phase B N-10.
killer_doubt: Direct back-tunneling through 1.5-2 nm oxide is temperature-insensitive (estimated retention of us to seconds), so 77 K cannot deliver hours, while LN2 cooling adds ~10-15% overhead.
decisive_experiment: Measure charge loss versus time at 300 K and 77 K on SONOS capacitors with 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5 nm tunnel oxides in a cryoprober; stop if the 77 K retention gain is below 10x. University fab, ~$100k.
prior_art: Tiwari et al. nanocrystal memory with ~2 nm oxide (IBM, APL 1996); Phase B N-10 direct-tunnel 3D AND; SNU CryoRAM model (ISCA 2019) (training knowledge).
